topics.label: Introduction to cancer evolution and lecture outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture theme and outlines the core learning outcomes concerning cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms in clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how intrinsic genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer selective advantages that drive clonal expansion and tumor initiation.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stem cell properties and tissue hierarchies influence the cell of origin and propagation across different cancer models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory drivers of tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how external stimuli, chronic inflammation, and supportive stromal interactions provide permissive signals required for tumor growth and persistence.

topics.label: Methods for investigating tumor evolution and microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the experimental and computational tools used to resolve the timing of mutations, cellular plasticity, and spatial organization within tumors.

topics.label: Integrated multifactorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes genetic, epigenetic, cell-of-origin, and microenvironmental factors into an overarching evolutionary framework of malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of upcoming session
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and provides framing for the next session on cancer therapy.
